content: Fixed-point simulation pitfalls: multiply/divide need a wider intermediate (64-bit for Q16.16, 128-bit for 64-bit formats) or silently wrap; sqrt via integer Newton iteration, sin/cos via LUT or CORDIC, never libm; Go and other runtimes use arch-specific assembly for sin/cos/sqrt so wasm vs native disagree; std::<random> distributions are implementation-defined so the same seed gives different sequences across libstdc++/libc++/MSVC; solver order dependence and map iteration order are classic desync sources.
